correctness.rationale: The minimum-degree first-force bound Z>=delta is sharp on each graph and equality determines any first-force seed B=N[v]\{w}; closed neighborhoods in the regular regime are length 2k+1 circular intervals. Explicit forcing grows such an interval to all n vertices. The 2k-subsets from adjacent neighborhoods account for exactly n duplicate two-presentations and no more, giving n(2k-1). Complete and K_n minus an antipodal perfect matching give n and nk respectively. A single token jump from any nonblock seed to a consecutive 2k-block, and a connected block backbone, prove full TJ connectivity. Independently recomputed all 65 pairs n=3..12, 4382 optimum-size candidate subsets, including actual color-change and full token-jump BFS; every predicted family and count matched.
residual_risks: The independent search exhausts only n<=12, while the infinite classification uses the neighborhood first-force and interval proof.
Only ordinary zero forcing and token-jump exchange, not skew/threshold forcing or token sliding.
